chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The most defiant of people toward God Almighty and Majestic is the one who killed someone other than his (attempted) killer, and the one who struck someone who did not strike him.'

key_terms.أَعْتَى: Most defiant/rebellious — the superlative of 'utuww (arrogant transgression); refers to the gravest moral and legal offenders
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — standard honorific epithet for God, emphasizing His power and greatness
key_terms.قَاتِلِهِ: His killer/attacker — the one who attempted or committed violence against him; the only legitimate target of qisas

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about killing someone who is not your attacker?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a prophetic saying that declares the most severely condemned people before God are those who engage in unlawful retaliation — specifically killing someone who was not their attacker, and striking someone who did not strike them. This hadith establishes a foundational principle of Islamic criminal law (qisas) and ethics: that retribution must be proportional and directed only at the actual aggressor. The audience of early Shia juristic scholars would have understood this as a direct prohibition of blood feuds and collective punishment, practices common in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The most trouble-maker of the people to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, is the one who killed someone other than his (attempted) killer, and the one who struck someone who did not strike him’.
